quote: Corse's brigade, of Pickett's division, with one regiment of North Carolina troops (of Pettigrew's brigade), remained at Hanover Junction.
note: Colonel Walter Taylor, of Lee staff, from the original returns of the army, on the brigade left away from Gettysburg.

quote: General Corse, who had been hurried forward with his brigade to secure the Gaps
note: Longstreet's report of the march to the Gaps after the battle (about 21 July 1863) names Brigadier-General Corse with his brigade; it says nothing of the brigade or its commander on 1 to 3 July, when it stayed at Hanover Junction.

change.detail: shot from his horse within about 25 paces of the stone wall

quote: He was shot from his horse while near the center of the brigade, within about 25 paces of the stone wall.
note: Peyton's report, after his remarks on General Garnett.

change.detail: commanded the brigade when Garnett fell and wrote its report

quote: Report of Maj. Charles S. Peyton, Nineteenth Virginia Infantry, commanding Garnetfs brigade, Pickett's division.
note: Heading of the report; the table prints him second under Garnett.

change.detail: killed in the cannonade before the advance

quote: Among the killed was Lieutenant-Colonel [John T.] Ellis, of the Nineteenth Virginia
note: Peyton's report.
Longstreet's list of officers distinguished in the battle.

change.detail: killed while leading his brigade, as Hunton writes

quote: Gen. Armistead was killed while actually leading his brigade with his hat on his sword.
note: Hunton's autobiography (written after the war). Hunton was wounded in the same charge and wrote what he knew; the Official Records in the local volume do not give Armistead's end.

change.detail: wounded at the red barn, a little more than half-way in the charge

quote: I was wounded at the red barn, a little more than half-way in the charge.
note: Hunton's own account, written after the war.

quote: The brigade went into action with 1,287 men and about 140 officers, as shown by the report of the previous evening
note: Peyton's report; the figure is that of the report of the evening of 2 July.

value.scope: regiment, men who went in the charge of 3 July

quote: The 8th Virginia Regiment, that carried into this charge an even two hundred men, as brave as ever carried musket - lost in killed, wounded and captured, one hundred and ninety.
note: Hunton, Autobiography: the Eighth Virginia, of which he was colonel. Hunton says elsewhere the regiment took position behind the artillery with 205 men in its ranks.

value.scope: regiment, in its ranks behind the artillery before the cannonade of 3 July

quote: The 8th took position just behind our artillery with 205 men in its ranks.
note: Hunton, Autobiography: the Eighth Virginia, of which he was colonel.

quote: The 8th Virginia Regiment, that carried into this charge an even two hundred men, as brave as ever carried musket - lost in killed, wounded and captured, one hundred and ninety.
note: Hunton, Autobiography: the Eighth Virginia, of which he was colonel. Killed, wounded and captured together; the return of casualties gives 54 (killed 6, wounded 48) and the Addenda 54 with no missing; the Addenda preface says many of the missing of Pickett division were killed or wounded.

quote: sustained a loss, as the list of casualties will show, of 941 killed, wounded, and missing
note: Peyton's report; the Addenda return prints 78 killed, 324 wounded and 539 captured or missing (941).

value.scope: brigade, during the cannonade before the advance

quote: During the shelling, we lost about 20 killed and wounded.
note: Peyton's report; 'about 20'.
